exercise.name: Alternating Hammer Curl
library_steps: Stand holding a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your body.
Curl one dumbbell up with your thumb on top, the other arm still.
Lower it and switch arms; both arms make one rep.
exercise.one_line_summary: Standing, a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing the body (thumbs forward, then thumbs up). Picture 1: left arm curled to ~124 deg, right hanging; picture 2: the reverse. Upper arms by the sides, no forearm turn.

setup.target: Feet hip-width, knees soft, trunk upright and still.
Neutral (palms facing the body/each other), thumb on top through the lift.
setup.tolerance: handle within 15 deg of square to the forearm, in the forward-up plane
setup.why: Library step; neutral grip is the hammer curl.

movement.joint: working elbow (left in picture 1, right in picture 2)

movement.end: facing in (thumb up toward the shoulder)

muscles.emg: Same activity with neutral as with supinated hand (no significant difference, S2)
Neutral = supinated share in unloaded flexion (S2); clearly active in loaded curls (S1)
muscles.role: Elbow flexor that is strongest in the mid (thumb-up) forearm position; the reason people pick this curl.
muscles.surface: Thumb side of the upper forearm.
Under the lower biceps, visible at the outer arm.

mistakes.mistake: Turning the palm up as it rises
mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Thumb rolls outward; becomes a normal curl.
mistakes.why_it_matters: Loses the neutral grip that defines the exercise.

mistakes.mistake: Elbow swinging forward / trunk leaning back
mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Upper arm leaves the side, body rocks.
mistakes.why_it_matters: Momentum and front delt instead of the elbow flexors.

sources.citation: Marcolin G, et al. 2018. Differences in electromyographic activity of biceps brachii and brachioradialis while performing three variants of curl. PeerJ 6:e5165.
sources.what_it_gave: Standing alternating dumbbell curl protocol: 65 % 1RM, 3 s reps, range 123 +- 12 deg, trunk policed; brachioradialis activity depends on forearm position.

sources.citation: Kleiber T, et al. 2015. Front Physiol 6:215, doi 10.3389/fphys.2015.00215 (EMG of biceps brachii and brachioradialis in elbow flexion by hand position).
sources.what_it_gave: 16 subjects, 0-130 deg, pronated / neutral / supinated: biceps unchanged; brachioradialis share higher in pronation; neutral = supinated.

sources.citation: American Council on Exercise. Exercise Library: Standing Bicep Curl.
sources.what_it_gave: Elbows close to the sides, hands toward the shoulders, lower slowly.

clip_check.check: Picture 1: left elbow 124 (115-135), right 13 (5-20); picture 2 reversed
Thumb on top of the curled dumbbell (handle in the forward-up plane)
clip_check.target: handle within 15 deg of the sagittal plane

clip_check.check: Hanging dumbbell clear of the thigh
Biceps is the strongest red in both pictures
